How Vehicle-Specific Fitment Works

Auto parts don't fit by make and model alone. Two vehicles from the same showroom floor — same badge, same year — can take different brake pads, water pumps or control arms if they left the factory with different engines. That's why this catalog is built on application data down to the engine level: every one of the 28,919,669 parts here is tied to the exact year, model and engine the manufacturer published fitment for, not a "may fit" guess.

Each part shows the brand, the manufacturer part number (MPN), and any position, trim or market qualifiers from the application record. That part number is your safety net: cross-reference it against the number stamped on the part coming off your vehicle, or against a dealer or repair-shop quote, before you order. When the numbers agree, the part fits — regardless of whether the box says OEM or aftermarket.

OEM and Aftermarket Coverage, Side by Side

The catalog lists original-equipment suppliers and aftermarket manufacturers together, so you can weigh a premium OE-grade part against an economy alternative for the same fitment. Where the data includes quality grades, parts are tagged so you can match the part to how the vehicle is actually used — a daily commuter, a work truck or a weekend classic don't need the same spec.

Coverage spans 1901 to 2027, which means plenty of vehicles here are long out of dealer support. For those, the part-number cross-reference matters even more: a discontinued OEM number can usually be traced to a current aftermarket equivalent through the parts on each vehicle's pages.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I find parts that fit my exact vehicle?

Start with your make, then choose the year, model and engine. Every part is matched to that full configuration, so the list you reach only includes parts with published fitment for your vehicle.

What vehicles does AutoFactsDB.com cover?

AutoFactsDB.com covers 301 makes from 1901 to 2027, across 28,853 year-and-engine configurations and 28,919,669 replacement parts. That includes everyday vehicles as well as older and discontinued ones.

Are these OEM parts or aftermarket parts?

Both. OE suppliers and aftermarket brands are listed together, each under its own part number. Fitment is checked at the engine level either way.

Can I look up a part by its part number instead?

Yes. Search a manufacturer part number to see the part, its brand, and the vehicles it fits — helpful when you already have a number from a box, invoice or old part.

Why does the catalog ask for my engine, not just my model?

Because fitment often follows the engine. Cooling, brake, suspension and drivetrain parts can differ between engines in the same model year. If you are unsure, check the under-hood emissions label or the 8th VIN character, then select that engine.
